summary: Rifaa'ah Zuraqi relates the Prophet's long du'aa of praise after Uhud as the Sahabah stood in rows, and Abdullaah bin Abbaas explains that some should stay behind on jihaad to learn Deen.
notes: Two reports joined: the du'aa after Uhud, and Ibn Abbaas's statement on learning while on jihaad. Rifaa'ah only relays the du'aa, so tagged narrator.

summary: Ahwas bin Hakeem bin Umayr Absi relates Umar's letter to the army commanders urging them to gain a deep understanding of Deen.

people.name: Ahwas bin Hakeem bin Umayr Absi

summary: Hitaan bin Abdullaah Raqaashi relates that Abu Moosa Ash'ari stopped people from renewing their wudu without need on the march and warned that knowledge would vanish and ignorance spread.
Abu Mas'ood Ansaari relates that a man donated a reined camel in the path of Allaah, and the Prophet promised him seven hundred camels in return on the Day of Qiyaamah.
Abdullaah bin Saamit relates how Abu Dharr spent his whole allowance in the path of Allaah, and the Prophet's warning that unspent gold and silver becomes live coal is quoted.
notes: Second paragraph is a separate report (Ahmad and Tabraani) carrying the same warning. Abdullaah bin Saamit's sahabi status is not stated in the text.

summary: Qais bin Sala Ansaari says his brothers complained that he gave away too much wealth, and the Prophet told him to keep spending so that Allaah would spend on him.
notes: Cut off mid-sentence at '(because of'.

summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal relays the Prophet's glad tidings of seventy thousand good deeds for dhikr while on jihaad, and explains that spending on the expedition itself earns the greater reward.
notes: Narrator Abdur Rahmaan is left unlinked: the approved 'abdur-rahmaan' may be the same person, but the text does not confirm it.

summary: Several Companions relay that spending while staying at home earns seven hundred times its reward and spending on an expedition seven hundred thousand times, and the Prophet recites Surah Baqara verse 261.
notes: The names from Abu Bakr to Aasim bin Adi come from a cross-reference to an earlier chapter on spending; tagged as mentioned.

summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that when a man asked about a fighter who seeks worldly gain, the Prophet said he receives no reward, and repeated this each time he was asked, three times in all.
Abu Umaamah relates that the Prophet said a man who fights for fame and fortune gets nothing, and that Allaah accepts only deeds done solely for His pleasure.
Aasim bin Amr bin Qataadah relates the story of Quzmaan, whom the Prophet named as one of the people of Jahannam, who fought fiercely at Uhud for his people's honour and then took his own life.
notes: Approved list has 'Aasim bin Umar bin Qataadah (no)', a different person; this narrator is marked RA, so kept separate. Quzmaan's sahabi status is not stated.

summary: Abu Hurayrah names Usayram as the man who entered Jannah without a single salaah, and Mahmood bin Labeed relates how he accepted Islaam on the day of Uhud and was martyred.
notes: Husayn, who asked Mahmood for the story, is not identified in the approved list and is not linked.

summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that Amr bin Uqaysh put off Islaam until his interest-bearing loans were repaid, then fought fiercely at Uhud, and when asked by Sa'd bin Mu'aadh's messenger he said he fought for Allaah and His Rasool.
notes: Sa'd bin Mu'aadh sent his sister to ask; she is not named in the text.

summary: Shaddaad ibnul Haad relates that a Bedouin who had followed the Prophet hoping for martyrdom was struck in the throat by an arrow exactly where he had pointed, and the Prophet led his janaazah.
Anas bin Maalik relates that a dark-skinned man who asked whether fighting would take him to Jannah was martyred, and the Prophet saw two wide-eyed damsels of Jannah disputing over his body.

Amr bin Al Aas says he accepted Islaam for love of Islaam and not for wealth, when the Prophet offered to send him in command of an army, and the Prophet replies that good wealth is a fine thing for a good man.
notes: The second paragraph is another version of the same exchange.

summary: Umar rebukes men who called their martyred comrades martyrs, saying every fighter is raised according to the intention he died with, and Maalik bin Aws relates the same teaching from Umar.
notes: Two reports joined: Abul Bakhtari's account of the Kufa gathering, and Maalik bin Aws's account of Umar's teaching (marked (I) in the text).

summary: Umar asks who the martyrs are, and when told they are those killed in battle, explains that the true martyr gives his life hoping for Allaah's reward, and defines the true Muhaajir and the true Muslim.
Asmaa tells her son Abdullaah bin Zubayr that if he fights to revive the Book and Sunnah he should die upon the truth, but if he seeks worldly gain there is no good in him, alive or dead.
notes: The approved list has Dimaam bin Tha'laba and Dimaad; not linked because the text does not say which.

summary: Abu Maalik Ash'ari relates that a man left the camp without the Ameer's permission, and Abu Moosa Ash'ari rebukes him and tells him to start afresh to undo his sin.
Abu Tha'laba Khushani relates that the Prophet called it Shaytaan's work when Muslims camped separately in valleys on expedition, and after that they always stayed together.

Another narrator adds that the Sahabah stayed so close that one sheet could cover them all, and Mu'aadh Juhani relates that the Prophet declared there is no reward in jihaad for one who crowds the camp or blocks a road.
notes: The first paragraph continues the report in n00621 (starts mid-story); the second is Mu'aadh Juhani's separate report.

summary: Sahl bin Handhaliyya relates that at Hunayn the Prophet asked for a night guard, Anas bin Abi Marthad Ghanawi volunteered and kept watch at the ravine, and the Prophet told him he had made Jannah compulsory for himself.

Abu Atiyya relates that when the Prophet was told a man had died, he asked whether anyone had seen good in him, and a Sahabi said he had stood guard with him, so the Prophet led the janaazah and testified that he was of Jannah.
new_themes: judging people by their good deeds

summary: Abu Atiyya and Abu Aa'idh relate that when some Companions asked the Prophet not to lead a janaazah, he asked whether anyone had seen any good deed by the dead man, and Umar objected that the man was sinful.
new_themes: judging people by their good deeds
notes: Abu Atiyya's report is cut short ('The Hadith continues further') before Abu Aa'idh's separate narration begins.

summary: Abu Rayhaana relates that the Prophet prayed for the volunteers who guarded the camp at night and said the eye that stands guard in the path of Allaah is safe from Jahannam, and Jaabir adds that Ammaar bin Yaasir and Abbaad bin Bishr guarded the mouth of the valley.
notes: Two reports: Abu Rayhaana's (given as a cross-reference to an earlier chapter) and Jaabir's account of the volunteers.

summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri relates that the Prophet said illness annuls sins, and Ubay bin Ka'b prayed for a fever that would never stop him from worship, and it stayed with him until his death.

Jundub bin Sufyaan relates that when the Prophet's finger bled from a fall, he said it was only a finger that bled and whatever it suffered was in the path of Allaah; Anas adds the injuries the Prophet took at Uhud.
notes: Ends with a cross-reference to Anas's report in another chapter; that report is not included here.

summary: Aa'isha relays Abu Bakr's account of Uhud: the Prophet told them to tend to Talha, who had over seventy wounds, and Abu Bakr said every credit for that day went to Talha.
notes: Excerpt from a longer Hadith related on Aa'isha's authority; begins mid-story.

summary: Ibraheem bin Sa'd reports that Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf sustained twenty-one wounds at Uhud, and an injury to his leg left him limping.

Anas bin Maalik relates how his uncle Anas bin Nadhar, who had missed Badr, fought at Uhud until he was martyred with over eighty wounds, and how the verse of Surah Ahzaab about men like him was revealed.
notes: The second paragraph is a fuller account of the same incident, not a separate report. Rubayyi bint Nadhar is named only in that paragraph.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar relates that the Prophet named Zaid bin Haaritha commander at Mu'ta with Ja'far and Abdullaah bin Rawaaha as successors, and that Ja'far's body had over ninety wounds, none on his back.
notes: The final paragraph is a variant of the same report. The vocabulary also has abdullaah-bin-rawwaaha for the same name; the first spelling is used here.

summary: Amr bin Shurahbeel relates that when Sa'd bin Mu'aadh was struck by an arrow at the Battle of the Trench and his blood spilled onto the Prophet, Abu Bakr and Umar cried out in shock.

Sa'eed bin Ubayd Thaqafi relates that he shot Abu Sufyaan bin Harb in the eye at Taa'if, and when Abu Sufyaan offered it as an injury in Allaah's path, the Prophet offered to pray for its return or give him Jannah, and he chose Jannah.
Qataadah bin Nu'maan relates that his eye was injured at Badr, and Rifaa'ah bin Raafi relates that an arrow ruptured his eye, which the Prophet treated with his saliva and prayer, leaving no pain.
notes: Two reports: Qataadah's (the rest is quoted in a later chapter) and Rifaa'ah's account from Badr, which names Umayyah bin Khalaf as the target.

summary: Raafi bin Khadeej asks the Prophet to remove an arrow from his chest, and separately a man from Banu Abdul Ash'hal and his wounded brother join the pursuit after Uhud, with the man carrying his brother at times.
notes: First paragraph is a cross-reference to a Hadith in an earlier chapter; the second is Abu Saa'ib's separate report. Yahya bin Abdul Hameed is left out (scholar named only in a reference line). Abu Saa'ib is not linked to the approved 'saaib'.

summary: Anas relates that during the battle against Musaylama, Baraa bin Maalik scaled an orchard wall and opened its gate, suffering over eighty wounds, and that Khaalid bin Waleed nursed him for a month.

Is'haaq bin Abdullaah bin Abu Talha relates that when Anas was being pulled up by a burning hook at an enemy fortress in Hareeq, Baraa bin Maalik held the chain until the rope gave way, burning his hand to the bone, and Allaah saved Anas.

people.name: Is'haaq bin Abdullaah bin Abu Talha

summary: Another narration says the hooks caught Anas and lifted him off the ground, and Baraa ran, jumped onto the wall and tugged the chain until the rope gave way, his hands burnt to the bone.
notes: Variant of n00638 with the same event; narrator not named.

summary: Abu Hurayrah relates that the Prophet swore he would have joined every expedition if not for men he could not provide transport for, and wished to be killed in the path of Allaah and given life again, repeatedly.
